body:
## Summary

Fixes #1166

Two changes, in both the native and the JavaScript roots:

1. **Typed obligations keep the issue's meaning.** The obligation binding no longer turns every mention of a literal into another output line, honours an explicit count, and leaves conditional outputs unbound.
2. **Independent acceptance.** A new checker reads only the task text and the candidate's files and observed output. It never sees the derivation that wrote the candidate, so a program and a test generated from the same misunderstanding are rejected together.

### What changed

| Area | Native | JavaScript (TS generated) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Output count and conditional outputs in obligations | `rust/src/intent_formalization/obligations.rs` (`explicit_count`, conditional literals unbound) | `js/agentic/crate/intent_formalization_obligations.mjs` |
| Output literals and conditions from task text | `rust/src/agentic_coding/task_condition.rs` | `js/agentic/task_condition.mjs` → `ts/agentic/task_condition.mts` |
| Per-clause verdicts, canonical meaning, task identity | `rust/src/agentic_coding/task_acceptance.rs` | `js/agentic/task_acceptance.mjs` → `ts/agentic/task_acceptance.mts` |
| Planner wiring: a finished recipe's answer carries the verdicts | `rust/src/agentic_coding/command_reroute.rs` (`recipe_step`) | `js/agentic/command_reroute.mjs` |
| Vocabulary (markers, relations, workflow and comment clauses) | seed roles in `data/seed/meanings-repository-workflow.lino` | same seed |
| Report wording | `data/meta/work-item-steps.lino` templates | same templates |

Every clause gets one of four verdicts, with a specific justification and the clause's byte span:

| Verdict | Example justifications |
| --- | --- |
| `discharged` | `output_matches`, `comments_present`, `workflow_path_matches` |
| `contradicted` | `output_differs`, `comments_missing`, `workflow_trigger_missing`, `workflow_path_differs` |
| `unresolved` | `workflow_status_unobserved`, `unread`, `judgment_required` |
| `inapplicable` | clauses that ask for nothing to check |

There is no generic "style satisfied" verdict. A clause that needs judgment ("clear", "best practices") stays `unresolved`. The report is `complete` only when no required clause is contradicted, and none is unresolved for any reason other than needing judgment.

Example: a finished recipe for the #1450 body whose program has no comments ends with:

```
Independent acceptance of the task: 14 discharged, 4 contradicted, 8 unresolved, 6 inapplicable.
- contradicted (comments_missing, bytes 192-230): Add clear comments explaining the code
- unresolved (judgment_required, bytes 234-290): Ensure the code follows Kotlin best practices and idioms
- contradicted (run_instructions_missing, bytes 294-375): If applicable, include build/run instructions in a comment at the top of the file
- unresolved (workflow_status_unobserved, bytes 817-856): Show a green check mark when tests pass
…
The task is not complete: a required clause above is contradicted or unresolved.
```
(`node experiments/issue-1166/print-bare-report.mjs` prints the full report.)

### Acceptance criteria → evidence

All cases live in one shared fixture, `rust/tests/fixtures/issue-1166/acceptance.json`. Both `rust/tests/unit/issue_1166_task_acceptance.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1166-task-acceptance.test.mjs` read it.

| Criterion | Fixture cases / tests |
| --- | --- |
| (a) repeated mentions → one line; `twice` → two | `once`, `restated`, `mentioned_twice`, `twice`; executed `restated_line_printed_once`, `twice_honoured` |
| (b) reversed comparisons, and/or, negation distinct | `distinctGroups`; executed `reversed_comparison_rejected`, `disjunction_for_conjunction_rejected`, `dropped_negation_rejected` (plus the `*_honoured` counterparts) |
| (c) comments, run instructions, workflow cannot be omitted | #1450 `candidateCases` (no comments, wrong output, other task, …); `a_finished_recipe_reports_only_actionable_verdicts` |
| (d) workflow file name, path, triggers, #1450's `ci/` | `under .github` and `no pull_request trigger` candidates; `workflow_triggers_are_read_in_every_yaml_form` |
| (e) exact Unicode, quotes, backslashes | `exact_backslash_unicode`, `exact_cyrillic_cjk`, `escaped_quote` (a gap, not a guess); executed `exact_backslash_unicode_kept`, `backslash_escape_misread` |
| (f) paraphrases share a meaning, unsupported grammar is a gap | `paraphraseGroups`; six `hello-world-kotlin-*` fixtures (en, paraphrase, es, ru, zh, hi) share one meaning; `unsupported_relation`; executed `unsupported_grammar_is_a_gap` |
| (g) JS/TS/native agree; a shared misunderstanding is rejected | the same fixture in both roots, TS held by `translate-es --check`; `shared_misunderstanding_of_twice` passes its own generated test and is still `contradicted (output_differs)` |
| Exact task identity | `task_identity = stable_id("task", text)`: one added newline gives a different identity |

The twelve Python candidates are actually executed, row by row over the condition's truth table, and only their stdout is observed.

### Supported subset (stated in the module headers)

```
statement := effect MARKER condition [SEP OTHERWISE effect]
           | MARKER condition SEP effect [SEP OTHERWISE effect]
condition := atom (CONNECTIVE atom)*     one connective kind per condition
atom      := operand [NEGATION] relation operand | operand symbol operand
operand   := identifier | integer
```

Checked clause kinds:
- output
- program file
- comments
- run instructions
- workflow: path, triggers, runs the program, verifies the output, runtime, observed status, file name, badge

Anything else is `unresolved (unread)`.

### Known limits

- Hindi conditional statements (verb-final) are outside the subset and stay a gap.
- Workflow branch filters are not read.
- Condition inputs are the identifiers in code-point order, passed as command-line arguments; the truth table uses the values 0..2.
- Comments are recognised by the language's line-comment prefix only.
- Run instructions must be in the leading comment block.
- A workflow's status needs an observed conclusion; without one the clause stays `unresolved`.
- Reader gaps (`unread`, `judgment_required`) do not add a report to an otherwise passing answer on their own, but stay visible in `check_task`.

### Verification status

- JavaScript: `node --test rust/tests/web/issue-1166-*.test.mjs` passes 32/32 locally, and the fast JS tiers pass in CI.
- TypeScript: `node scripts/translate-es.mjs --check` passes locally (714 files), and the ts tier passes in CI.
- Native compile: `cargo check --tests` is clean locally with no errors or warnings, and CI's native type and lint check passes.
- **Native unit tests were not executed.** `rust/tests/unit/issue_1166_task_acceptance.rs` and `issue_1166_executor_gaps.rs` compile but have not been run:
  - Linking the test binary needs a codegen build of the `formal_ai` lib. On the machine that prepared this PR, the 3 GB cgroup killed that build at opt-level 2, at opt-level 0 and without incremental compilation (memory peak equal to the limit).
  - `--no-default-features` does not build on `main` either.
  - Pull-request CI only type-checks Rust. The native unit suite runs on `main`.
- So the native leg of criterion (g) is verified by compilation and the shared fixture only, not by execution. It needs one `cargo test --test unit issue_1166` run on a larger machine before merge.

### How to reproduce the original bug

Take the #1450 body (`rust/tests/fixtures/issue-1166/issue-1450-body.md`) and a candidate that:
- has no comments,
- writes `.github/workflows/*.yml` instead of `ci/`, or
- prints the restated line twice.

Before this change the run was reported done. Now each of these clauses is `contradicted`, with its span, and the answer says the task is not complete.

### Docs

- Requirement rows R1166-9 … R1166-16 in `docs/requirements/issue-1166-request-formalization.md`, the traceability rows, and the regenerated ledger and assembled register. The shard moved to the "coding and agents" part because the reasoning part reached its 1400-line limit.
- `docs/case-studies/issue-1166/README.md` (independent acceptance section)
- `changelog.d/20261116_120000_issue_1166_task_acceptance.md`
- New seed role and template names use `-` (the notation ratchet).

### Unrelated CI repair included here

`data/benchmarks/fast-pull-request-javascript-tests.json` on `main` is missing a comma after `stale-pull-request-report.test.mjs` (lost in a merge). Because of this, every fast JS tier fails while parsing the manifest. This PR restores the comma.

The shared acceptance fixture is laid out compactly (same data, checked by `experiments/issue-1166/format-acceptance-fixture.mjs`) so that it stays under the 1500-line limit for maintained files.

`docs/architecture/module-map.md` on `main` is missing the `meta_executor` row added by #1550, so the module-map check fails. This PR regenerates the map with `node scripts/generate-module-map.mjs --write`.

The native fence and interpreter checks read their prefixes from data instead of string literals: `owned-clause-fence-prefixes` and the new `script-interpreter-prefix` key in `data/meta/work-item-steps.lino`. This keeps the `literal-predicates` debt ceiling at 432 (measured 432).

The nineteen meanings that only the task-acceptance clause reader uses (`code-comment-obligation`, `workflow-trigger-pull-request`, `condition-marker`, …) also carry `role scoped-grammar-pattern`. That keeps them out of the general text-formalization meaning index, as is already done for the calculator's grammar frames. Without it, the new phrase "pull request" changed how two issues in the dependency-summarization corpus are read, and three ratchet measures fell by 0.001. With it, the measures match `main` exactly. `experiments/issue-1166/summarization-per-document.mjs` diffs the corpus document by document between two trees.

The governed Unicode-identifier witness records the bytes of `rust/src/intent_formalization.rs` and `rust/tests/unit/mod.rs`, which this PR changes. It was refreshed with the test's `--refresh-reviewed-baseline` mode after `experiments/issue-1571/governed-witness-delta.mjs` showed the only differences were those 13 fixture hashes.
title: fix: preserve complete issue meaning in typed obligations and independent acceptance (#1166)

body:
## Summary

Fixes #1558

The merge of #1563 (the #1558 implementation) and #1569 (#1487 statement identity) left `main` red. This PR restores every main gate those merges broke.

### 1. The Rust crate compiles again (`E0308`)
`ProofOutcome::confidence` (added for #1487 in `rust/src/proof_engine/types.rs`) returned `f64`. Its only caller passes that value to `finalize_simple`, which takes `f32`. So every Rust lane on `main` failed with:

```
error[E0308]: mismatched types
  --> rust/src/solver_handlers/user_intent.rs:141
```

It now returns `f32`, the type the `match` it replaced used to infer. The `E0308` failed these on `main` (686367d20), and the fix unblocks all of them:
- doc tests
- *Build binaries and tests*
- lint lanes 1–4
- the scheduled *Task Ladder* and *Write-Effect Ladder* workflows

### 2. tests-as-docs gate (R234-2)
The gate rejected `negated_theorem_request_is_refuted_never_proven` (`rust/tests/unit/proof_request.rs`) because it had no exact-answer assertion. It now pins the full refutation answer with `assert_eq!(response.answer, "…")`. I checked `scripts/check-tests-as-docs.rs` on both trees: it fails on the base tree and passes with this change.

### 3. JS/Rust parity for Euclid proof requests (#1487)
Pinning the exact native answer showed that the JavaScript worker disagreed with it in two ways:
- **Refutation.** "Prove there are not infinitely many primes." embedded the positive theorem's `Proof (method: contradiction).` block, which the native test forbids.
- **Affirmed proof.** It was a hand-written copy for each language, without step labels.

Both are now rendered from the seeded theorem (`proofLibraryTheoremProof`) with the shared presenter helpers. The refutation is a `Disproof` with labelled steps and the native clarifying-question footer (`proofPresenterDisprovenFollowUps`), byte-identical to `render_disproven` plus `enforce_questions`.

`rust/tests/web/issue-1487-proposition-identity.test.mjs` pins both exact answers. It also asserts that no negated request (EN/ZH) carries a `Proof (` / `证明 (` heading.

Supporting changes:
- The TS twins are regenerated with `scripts/translate-es.mjs --write`.
- Worker line budget for `formal_ai_worker_calendar_and_proofs`: 1208 → 1146.
- JS literal ratchet `worker-ceiling`: 429 → 416. Both numbers only fall.

### 4. Merge reconciliation
- Adopted main's fixture layout (`rust/tests/fixtures/`) and module order.
- Dropped the duplicate `mod` declaration the merge produced.

### Experiments / tooling
- `experiments/issue-1558/rust-module-harness/` compiles the unchanged `rust/src/agentic_coding/work_item_references.rs` and its unit tests on their own (9/9 pass), without building the whole crate.
- `experiments/plan-event-append-race/stress.sh` investigates the intermittent `simultaneous retries take the bounded lock and retain exactly one event` failure on main. It did not reproduce in 0/1,500 concurrent runs, so no code change is made for it.
- `experiments/issue-1558/negated-theorem-answer.mjs` prints the worker's intent, answer and evidence for a prompt.

### Out of scope
- `dependencies-latest` fails on main because of about 50 upstream dependency bumps. That failure has nothing to do with #1558/#1487 and existed before them.

### Caveat
PR CI does not compile Rust; only `main` does. The native assertions are therefore checked by `cargo check`/`rustfmt` locally and by the byte-identical JavaScript answer. They are exercised in full by the main pipeline after merge.

## Verification (local)
- `node --test rust/tests/web/issue-1487-proposition-identity.test.mjs`: 10/10 pass.
- `rust-script scripts/check-tests-as-docs.rs` (built as a cargo project): fails on the base tree, passes here.
- `node scripts/translate-es.mjs --check`, `check-js-literals`, and the worker line-budget gate pass.
- `cargo fmt --check` passes, and `cargo check --test unit` compiles the unit test target (including the new `assert_eq!`) with no errors or warnings.
- `experiments/issue-1558/rust-module-harness`: `cargo test` 9/9.
- `experiments/plan-event-append-race/stress.sh`: 0 duplicates in 1,500 runs.
title: fix(ci): restore the main gates broken by the #1558/#1487 merges (f32 confidence, tests-as-docs, Euclid JS/Rust parity)

body:
Fixes #1560

## Summary

In three Hive Mind drafts (PRs 1498, 1499 and 1502, on issues 1486, 1489 and 1501), the session summary was a raw `repository-work-item-evidence/v1` JSON object with `"reason":"ReadPolicyRefused"` and `"observations":[]`. For 1501, the requirement text was the signed-out GitHub page, with its chrome. With this PR the same sessions read repository files and end with a localized report. The JSON record stays in the trace.

## How to reproduce (before this PR)

Use the recorded Hive Mind tool set and user turn in `data/benchmarks/fixtures/work-item-1560/`. Give the agent the text of issue 1486, 1489 or 1501 as the output of the `gh issue view` read, then let it plan to its final answer (`node experiments/issue-1560/session-outcome.mjs`). On `main`:

- every read is refused (`ReadPolicyRefused`, no observations);
- the final answer is the serialized record;
- for 1501 the `<untrusted_context>` receipt quoted in the issue body made the `gh` read look "not work-item shaped". The agent then fetched the GitHub page, and its title, "Skip to content" and "Sign in" became the requirement.

## Root causes and fixes (one commit each)

| Commit | Root cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| f7a4bba90 | The envelope parser took the first `<untrusted_context>` tag anywhere in the tool output, so a receipt *quoted inside* issue 1501 replaced the real `gh issue view` result. | A harness envelope must frame the whole result (JS `tool_result.mjs`, Rust `tool_result.rs` / `source_observation.rs`). |
| 8b07de6bd | `read_policy_blocks_plan(task, …)` was run over the fetched issue text. A long issue that talks about not reading things refused every read. | The evidence collector, boundary controller and file-I/O lowering check the policy against the **latest user turn**. The task is used only when there is no user turn. |
| 127a1ae54 | A fetched page was accepted whole, and only raw markup was rejected. | `work_item_page` keeps only the title (without ` · GitHub`) and the issue body. The markers are data in `data/meta/work-item-steps.lino`. A page with no issue body (sign-in page) is rejected, so the REST and `gh api` reads of #1155 run instead. |
| 3ab326a18 | `finish` returned `AgenticPlan::Final(payload.to_string())`, and the whole issue was one `unbound` requirement. | The issue is split into Markdown-block requirements **before** evidence is read. The record is rendered by `work_item_report` through localized seeds (`multilingual-responses-agentic-workspace.lino`) into what stopped the session, which files it read, what it needs, which requirement a refusal concerns, and the requirements still unverified. |
| dbe068b44 | The boundary candidate, observed-documentation and source-repair finals were also serialized records. | They are rendered the same way. In repository work-item mode, any final that parses as a JSON object goes through the report (`reported_work_item_final`). |
| f0fc7f1f6 / 6231f495a | Tests and the qualification oracle parsed the answer as JSON. | Tests read the record from the final result instead: JS `workItemRecordOf(plan)`, Rust `reported_work_item_record(answer)`. The server's `agent.terminal` event carries `work_item_record`. The trace oracle gets the record back by replay. |
| 747ddce3a | A Markdown link label such as `build-hive-original-delivery-image.mjs` was read at the repository root and failed. | A bare file name that the work item's own GitHub blob link places in the repository is read at the linked path. After merging `main`, #1558's `work_item_references` does this, so the merge keeps that resolver and drops this PR's narrower `linked_evidence_paths`. The refusal and record handling of this PR are applied to `main`'s collector. |
| 818794ea6 | The issue-1133 page fixtures had only chrome and were used as the objective. | The fixtures now have a real issue body between the chrome. |
| a3f812ce3 | The requirement splitter's fence test added two literal predicates (debt ratchet 439 > 437). | A fence is recognized by its first three characters, with no literal predicate. |
| f3a0639b6 | The 11 new report intents had no authored meaning (closure gap 1046 > 1035). | They are grounded in `data/seed/meanings-engine-report-intents.lino`, which points to the agentic-workspace shard. |
| 4d863115a | `workItemRecordOf` had no named Rust twin (planner-twin ratchet 1 > 0). | Its doc comment names `reported_work_item_record` as its twin. |
| 57aca6c3b | The new report intents, response ids and page-marker keys used underscores (notation ratchet). | They are spelled with dashes, like the neighbouring keys in the same files. |
| de21fe336 | The #1558 resolver required a path to start with an alphanumeric, so issue 1486's link to `.github/workflows/hive-mind-draft.yml` was dropped and the glob match filtered out. The session ended `UnresolvedReferences` for a file the repository holds. | A segment may start with a dot. `.` and `..` are still never segments. |
| 6c4294b5c | For a bare name, the exact-path bonus went only to targets with a directory, so for 1501 a depth-6 `compiled-first-slice/README.md` beat the root `README.md` on the shared word "first". | The exact path always ranks first, as the resolver's documented order says. |
| 7a8374b24 | After merging `main`, rustfmt wanted the new test module declared after #1558's. | The module order follows rustfmt. |

## Tests (both runtimes)

- **New, JS:** `rust/tests/web/work-item-report-outcome.test.mjs`. 10 tests, in the fast PR list.
- **New, Rust twin:** `rust/tests/unit/agentic-coding/work_item_report_outcome.rs`.
- Both drive recorded Hive Mind sessions to their final answer and check:
  - **1486, 1489, 1501:** the issue is read first, at least one repository file is read completely, the final is not a JSON object, the reason is not `ReadPolicyRefused`, the report names the file it read, and the issue is split into more than one requirement.
  - **1501 page:** `work_item_page_text` keeps only the title and body. A fetch-only session reads a file, and no requirement or answer contains "· GitHub", "Skip to content" or "Sign in".
  - **Sign-in page:** it is rejected (`None`/`null`), a REST or `gh api` read follows the webfetch, and the session continues from the API body.
  - **User turn:** "Do not read package.json. Investigate package.json." is still honoured.
  - **Refusal:** the localized refusal names the requirement it concerns.
  - **1486:** the link into `.github/workflows/` is read at its linked path, nothing is left unresolved, and the reason is `EvidenceCollected`.
  - **1501:** a bare `README.md` is the root file, not a deeper one whose directory shares a word with the text.
  - Each of the last two fails before its fix and passes after it.
- **Tests that pinned the old behaviour now check the outcome:**
  - `agentic_general_planner.rs` (issue 698 replay);
  - `work-item-evidence.test.mjs`, `source-repair-intake.test.mjs`, `issue_1133_hive_mind_three_runs.rs`, `atomic-record-append-contract.test.mjs`;
  - documentation, boundary and hosted-effects tests;
  - `agent_cli_entry_point.rs`.

Session outcomes measured with `experiments/issue-1560/session-outcome.mjs`:

| Issue | Files read | Final reason | Answer is JSON |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1486 | `scripts/build-hive-original-delivery-image.mjs`, `.github/workflows/hive-mind-draft.yml` | `EvidenceCollected` | no |
| 1489 | `scripts/self-hosting-metric.rs`, `js/provenance/full-verifier.mjs` | `EvidenceCollected` | no |
| 1501 | `js/server/main.mjs`, `README.md` | `EvidenceCollected` | no |

## Acceptance mapping

- [x] For 1486, 1489 and 1501 the session reads at least one repository file, and none ends with `ReadPolicyRefused`. Covered by `hive_mind_sessions_read_a_repository_file_and_do_not_refuse_the_read` and its JS twin.
- [x] No work-item final parses as a JSON object. `reported()` in both outcome tests asserts it, and `reported_work_item_final` enforces it in repository work-item mode.
- [x] The 1501 requirement text has no "· GitHub", "Skip to content" or "Sign in". Covered by the 1501 page tests.
- [x] A page without an issue body is rejected and the fallback is used. Covered by `a_page_without_an_issue_body_is_rejected_and_the_api_read_is_used`.
- [x] A user turn that says not to read a file is honoured. Covered by `a_user_turn_that_says_not_to_read_a_file_is_still_honoured`.

## Assumptions and known limits

- **Where the record lives.** Step 1 of the issue says to keep the JSON "in the trace and in the plan file". The record is kept:
  - in the trace: Rust `[trace] work_item_record=…`, plus `reported_work_item_record` / `latest_work_item_record` for in-process callers;
  - on the JS final result: `result.record`, and the `agent.terminal` event's `work_item_record`.

  No plan file is written, because these sessions must not write an auxiliary plan journal (the existing `PLAN_PATH` assertion). The qualification oracle recovers the record by replay, and its verdict is "unknown" when it cannot.
- **`Node.js` in issue 1501** is a product name, not a file, after merging #1558. It is reported as a term, and the collector no longer stops at its failed read.
- **Local verification.**
  - **JavaScript:** the full fast PR list (`scripts/list-fast-pull-request-tests.mjs`, 186 files) was run serially at 7a8374b24: 183 pass and 3 fail. The 3 failures come from this sandbox's dependency set, not from this PR, and fail the same way on `main`: `census-source-selectors` (2), `release-trigger-paths` (7, the owned YAML block sequence is not parsed) and `patched-matcher-compatibility` (the `minimatch-modern` package is not installed). PR CI is green on the same commit.
  - **Governance:** these checks pass locally: debt and literal-predicate ratchets, closure audit, planner twins, role registry, seed metadata, response parity debt, file size, hardcoded language, data mirror, and `translate-js-rust --verify`.
  - **Rust (blocked locally):**
    - The tests compile: `cargo check -j1 --tests` of the lib and the `unit` test target passes with no warnings, and rustfmt passes on every changed Rust file.
    - They could not be run here. Every build of the test binaries was OOM-killed (SIGKILL) in the 2.9 GB sandbox, including the latest try at `opt-level` 0 with `codegen-units=256`, `debug=0` and incremental off. One of these kills is the container OOM notice posted on this PR.
    - PR CI cannot run them either, because the release.yml test jobs are gated to `main`. So `work_item_report_outcome.rs` and the updated Rust tests will first run on `main`. Their JS twins pass locally.
title: fix: render work-item records as localized reports, read policy over the user turn, and keep only an issue page's title and body

body:
## Summary

A work item that names a file now gets that file read where it actually lives, and the session ends with an evidence report instead of the repetition guard. Each name is resolved in this order: the exact path first, then a unique match by file name (glob, or `find` when only a shell is available), then at most three candidates ranked by how similar their path is to the words around the reference. A known product or runtime name with no match (`Node.js`) is recorded as a term. A file in another repository becomes one explicit unresolved item. A read that failed, or one that already succeeded, is never planned again.

Fixes #1558

## Root causes

Measured by replaying the recorded Agent CLI request (`data/benchmarks/fixtures/issue-1558/agent-cli-request.json`) through the server entry with `experiments/issue-1558/replay-session.mjs`.

| | Cause | Effect in the transcripts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | `Progress.sourceReadFor(path)` (`js/agentic/progress.mjs:317`, twin `Progress::source_read_for`) matches a read by exact string equality. The planner plans `path: "scripts/x.mjs"`, but the server binds the call to the client as `{"filePath":"<workspace>/scripts/x.mjs"}`. The recorded read never equals the planned path, so the planner plans the same read again. | The same read three times, then "Repeated action stopped". This explains both the successful case of link-assistant/hive-mind#4033 / PR 4040 (comment on this issue) and the failed reads. |
| B | The read tool answers `Error: File not found: …` as normal output, not as an error. It was not recognised as a failed read. | A missing file counted as "observed", and nothing else was tried. |
| C | `workItemEvidencePaths` took every word that looks like a file name as a path at the workspace root. It had no file-name search, no handling of `github.com/<owner>/<repo>/blob/<ref>/<path>` links, and no distinction between product names and files. | `hive-delivery-attempt.mjs` was read at the root instead of `scripts/`, `Node.js` was read as a file, and Hive Mind files were looked up in this repository. |

## What changed

- `js/agentic/work_item_references.mjs` (new) and its twin `rust/src/agentic_coding/work_item_references.rs`:
  - reference extraction: link text resolves to the linked path; links to other repositories are marked external with their repository;
  - `PRODUCT_NAMES`;
  - path comparison that treats the relative and absolute bindings as the same path;
  - search actions: glob `**/<name>`, or a bounded `find . -type f -name '<name>'` that excludes `node_modules` and `.git`;
  - parsing of search results and candidate ranking by path similarity to the context words;
  - `File not found` / `ENOENT` detection.
- `js/agentic/work_item_evidence.mjs` and `rust/src/agentic_coding/work_item_evidence.rs`: the evidence loop.
  - Every reference goes through exact read, then search, then up to three candidate reads, and ends either read or as a term or unresolved item. A reason is recorded for every unresolved item: `OutsideRepository`, `SearchUnavailable`, `SearchFailed`, `NotFound`, `CandidatesUnreadable`.
  - The other references are still read.
  - The final report adds `unresolved` and `terms`, and its reason is `EvidenceCollected`, `UnresolvedReferences` or `IncompleteSourceObservation`.
- `scripts/work-item-qualification/trace-oracle.mjs` accepts `UnresolvedReferences` as an explicit gap terminal.
- `ts/agentic/*.mts` is regenerated with `node scripts/translate-es.mjs --write`.

The repetition guard (`repeatedActionStop` / `repeated_action_stop`) is unchanged. A test asserts it still stops a repeated action, and every session test asserts it is not what ends these sessions.

## Reproduction

```bash
# Before (main) and after: the actions planned for the five recorded issues against this checkout
node experiments/issue-1558/simulate-session.mjs 1485 1487 1507 1484 1488
# The recorded Agent CLI request replayed through the server entry
node experiments/issue-1558/replay-session.mjs data/benchmarks/fixtures/issue-1558/agent-cli-request.json
# The link-assistant/hive-mind#4033 case and a change request naming an existing file
node experiments/issue-1558/simulate-hive-mind-4033.mjs
node experiments/issue-1558/simulate-change-request.mjs
```

Output on this branch (abridged):

| Issue | Reads | Final report |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1485 | `scripts/hive-delivery-attempt.mjs` | `EvidenceCollected` |
| 1487 | `js/agentic/crate/text_formalization.mjs` + 4 other named files | `EvidenceCollected` |
| 1507 | glob `**/Node.js` (no match), then 5 named files; `Node.js` is never read | `EvidenceCollected`, `terms: ["Node.js"]` |
| 1484, 1488 | none: every file is in link-assistant/hive-mind | `UnresolvedReferences`, one `OutsideRepository` item per file |

On `main`, the same sessions read the names at the workspace root, repeated the read and ended with "Repeated action stopped".

## Tests

The fixtures are the five recorded issue texts and the hive-mind 4033 work item in `data/benchmarks/fixtures/issue-1558/`.

- **JS** `rust/tests/web/issue-1558-reference-resolution.test.mjs` (13 tests; helper `rust/tests/web/helpers/issue-1558-session.mjs`, listed in `fast-pull-request-javascript-tests.json`). It drives full sessions through `planChatStep` against this checkout or a virtual workspace:
  - 1485 and 1487 read the linked paths;
  - 1507 does not read `Node.js`;
  - 1484 and 1488 report each external file once as unresolved;
  - a bare name is searched and the nearest candidate is read;
  - a failed read is searched once, then reported unresolved, and the remaining evidence is still read;
  - the search falls back to the shell when there is no glob tool;
  - an external reference does not stop the session;
  - hive-mind 4033: `src/solve.results.lib.mjs` is read once under its absolute binding;
  - a work item that names an existing file and asks for a change in it reads the file once;
  - the repetition guard stays in place.

  Every session asserts that no call is repeated and that the guard does not fire.
- **Rust**
  - `rust/tests/unit/agentic-coding/issue_1558_reference_resolution.rs` covers the same cases through `create_chat_completion_with_solver` with an agent-mode solver. It emulates the Agent CLI read/glob/bash answers, including `Error: File not found: <abs>`. (11 tests; type-checked by clippy, not executed yet, see the Rust note below.)
  - `rust/tests/unit/agentic-coding/work_item_references.rs` contains unit tests of extraction, product names, ranking and not-found detection. Its expected values were cross-checked against the JS output. These 6 tests are included in the module as `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` and **pass** through the harness below.
  - `experiments/issue-1558/rust-module-harness`: `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/target-1558-harness cargo test --manifest-path experiments/issue-1558/rust-module-harness/Cargo.toml` runs the real `work_item_references.rs` with those 6 tests plus 3 dedup checks. Result: 9/9 pass. It needs a few hundred MB, not the full crate.
- `rust/tests/web/work-item-evidence.test.mjs`: a failed read with no search tool now ends as `UnresolvedReferences` (`SearchUnavailable`) instead of `IncompleteSourceObservation`.

## Interpretation notes

- **"An external reference is reported once as unresolved and the session continues."** The other references of the same work item are still read after the external one is recorded (test: "an external reference does not stop the session"). When every reference is external (1484, 1488), nothing in this repository remains to be read. The session then ends with the `UnresolvedReferences` evidence report rather than with the guard.
- **Search before giving up.** At most one search and at most three candidate reads are made per reference, so a work item with eight names stays bounded.
- **Rust: what ran and what did not.** CI on pull requests does not compile Rust. The Rust build, clippy and tests in `release.yml` and `layered-ci.yml` require `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`, also under `workflow_dispatch`. The solver container has a 3.1 GB memory limit, and the 324k-line crate cannot be code-generated in it: at `-j 1` and opt-level 0, rustc passes 2.2 GB, with LLVM and with Cranelift alike. An earlier attempt OOM-killed the session. What did run locally:
  - **Clippy** with the CI flags (`--lib --tests`, `-D warnings`, `-D clippy::correctness/suspicious/perf`) passes. This type-checks the twin and both new Rust test files.
  - **`experiments/issue-1558/rust-module-harness`** compiles the unchanged `rust/src/agentic_coding/work_item_references.rs` together with its in-crate unit tests, and replaces only the three sibling modules it uses. **9/9 pass**: the 6 in-crate tests run against the recorded issue texts, and 3 more tests cover a relative path matching a workspace-bound read, `File not found` counting as a failure, and a search already answered.
  - rustfmt, the hardcoded-language lint and the planner twin ratchet also pass.
  - **Not executed:** `cargo test --test unit issue_1558`, the full-session Rust tests that go through `create_chat_completion_with_solver`. They type-check, but they first run in the main-branch Rust tier, or with `cargo test --test unit issue_1558` on a machine with more memory. The JS twin of these sessions runs and passes in PR CI.
  - Running the Rust tier on pull requests would close this gap; see https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md.
title: fix(agentic): resolve file names from a work item before reading them, and never plan the same read twice (#1558)

body:
## Summary

An English issue was answered in Spanish ("Planificado, no ejecutado") or Russian. There were two causes, and this PR fixes both in the Rust crate, its JS twin and the browser worker fallback.

Fixes #1557

### Root cause

1. **Markers matched as substrings.** The Spanish markers in `data/seed/language-detection.lino` use the Latin script, which English shares. They were found with a plain substring search, so the English words "formalization", "described" and "response" counted as the Spanish markers "formaliza", "escribe" and "responde". Three such hits were enough to call an English issue Spanish (issues 1235, 1446 and 1548).
2. **The whole fetched issue decided the language.** The answer of a repository work item used `detect(plan.goal)`. The execution layer replaces the goal with the fetched issue text, so a quoted Russian sentence, a Russian code block or a Russian title could switch an English issue to Russian (issues 1330 and 1396). The user's own turn was never consulted.

### Fix

- **Whole-word markers.** A marker of a script several languages share counts only when no letter is directly before or after it. This applies in `rust/src/language.rs` (`marker_count`), `js/agentic/crate/language.mjs` (`markerCount`) and `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_seed_responses_and_language.js` (`markerWordIn`). Markers in a script only one language uses (Cyrillic, Devanagari, Han) are unchanged.
- **Prose detection.** `detect_prose` / `detectProse` first remove fenced code, `>` quote lines, code spans, quotations, URLs and identifier-like tokens (paths, `snake_case`, `camelCase`, `::`). They then decide by proportion:
  - A language with its own script wins if its letters are at least 1/6 of the shared-script letters.
  - Spanish wins if its votes are at least 1/10 of the words. A vote is a whole-word marker or a word with a Spanish accented letter. A single vote must also be at least half of the words, so one marker or one accented loanword ("café") cannot flip a short English sentence, while "hola", "gracias" or "formaliza esto" still read as Spanish.
  - Otherwise the fallback language (English) wins.
  - With no prose left, there is no answer, and the next source is tried.
- **Markup markers are seed data.** The fence markers (```` ``` ````, `~~~`) and link markers (`://`, `www.`) that prose detection drops live in a new `prose-syntax` record of `data/seed/language-detection.lino` (mirrored to `rust/embedded/`), not in Rust or JS literals. This keeps the `literal-predicates` debt ceiling at 437.
- **Priority of sources.** For a repository work item, `GeneralChangePlan::response_language()` / `planResponseLanguage()` use, in order:
  1. the language of the user's own turn, recorded as `request_language` when the turn is more than the work-item reference;
  2. the prose of the issue body;
  3. the prose of the title;
  4. as before, `detect(goal)`.

  A forced language still wins over all of them. Rust and JS use the same method in `general_execution` as in the planned-not-executed answer.

### Reproduction

`experiments/issue-1557-replay.mjs` replays a Hive Mind work-item request (`<issue URL>\n\nProceed.`) whose `fetch_url` returns the real body of issue 1548:

```
node experiments/issue-1557-replay.mjs . rust/tests/fixtures/issue-1557-attempted-issues.json 1548
# before (be8ce8046): Planificado, no ejecutado: https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/904.
# after:              Planned, not executed: https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/904.
```

### Tests

- `rust/tests/fixtures/issue-1557-attempted-issues.json` is the regression fixture. It holds the bodies of the 19 attempted issues (1235, 1328, 1330, 1364, 1395, 1396, 1438, 1446, 1455, 1483–1489, 1501, 1507, 1548), all expected English, built by `experiments/issue-1557-build-fixture.mjs`. It also holds six synthetic cases:
  - a fully Russian issue → ru
  - a Russian body with English identifiers → ru
  - an English body containing "formalization", "described" and "response" → en
  - an English body quoting a Russian sentence → en
  - an English body with a Russian code block and blockquote → en
  - a fully Spanish issue → es
- `rust/tests/web/issue-1557-prose-language.test.mjs` has 12 tests and is added to the fast pull-request lane. They cover:
  - every fixture case;
  - issues 1235, 1446 and 1548 being English in the planner;
  - issues 1330 and 1396 being English while a Russian issue stays Russian;
  - that no Latin-script marker matches as a prefix;
  - that a single marker or a quotation does not outvote the prose;
  - that es/ru/hi/zh detection is unchanged;
  - the priority of turn, then body, then title;
  - an end-to-end replay that asserts `Planned, not executed`;
  - the worker fallback detector.
- `rust/tests/integration/issue_1557_prose_language.rs` is the Rust mirror of the same cases. It is registered in the integration crate, because `rust/tests/unit/mod.rs` is pinned by the governed unicode-identifier witness (`governed-baseline.v8`) that the Layered CI checks.
- `experiments/issue-1557-seed-loader-parse.mjs` parses the seed with the browser's `js/seed_loader.js`. The new `prose-syntax` record parses cleanly, and `extractLanguageRules` still returns the same five rules (ru, hi, zh, es, en). `rust/src/seed.rs::language_rules` also reads only `rule` children.
- `experiments/issue-1557-short-inputs.mjs` prints `detectProse`, `detect` and `proseOf` for any texts given as arguments, to probe short inputs.

Run locally, all passing: the new test (12/12), `worker-unknown-language`, `issue-1185-fourteen-languages`, `fetch-work-item-observations`, `fast-pull-request-production-profile`, `scripts-js-twins-checks`, `scripts-js-twins-language-parity`, `language-test-coverage` and `feature-capability-languages`. Also passing: `worker-crate-reexports`, `worker-factory-layout`, `worker-module-inventory`, `r999-worker-budget-rationale`, `requirement-listing-route`, `rust-specification-fixture-integrity` and `rust-specification-unicode-identifiers`. These gates also pass: `node scripts/translate-js-rust.mjs --verify`, `generate-worker-crate-modules.mjs --check`, `mirror-package-data.mjs --check`, `check-debt-ratchet.mjs --base origin/main`, `translate-es.mjs --check`, `generate-source-cst-runtime.mjs --check`, the notation ratchet (`notation.test.mjs`), `check-file-size`, `check-hardcoded-language`, `check-worker-line-budget` and `check-readable-code`. `check-source-duplication.mjs` needs `@babel/parser`, which is not installed locally, so it is left to CI.

**Not verified locally:** I did not compile Rust. CONTRIBUTING says "do not build or test Rust locally", so only `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` was run on the changed Rust files. The Rust unit test and the Rust changes are checked by CI.

### Also in this PR

- `ts/` is regenerated from `js/` with `node scripts/translate-es.mjs --write` (`ts/agentic/crate/language.mts`, `ts/agentic/general_execution.mts`, `ts/agentic/general_planner.mts` and two worker files). The Layered CI `ts tier` checks it with `--check`.

- `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_crate_language.js` is the browser worker's generated copy of `language.mjs`, regenerated with `generate-worker-crate-modules.mjs --write`. Its reviewed ceiling in `data/meta/worker-line-budget/formal_ai_worker_crate_language.lino` rises from 291 to 474 lines, the exact size of the regenerated factory, and the shard explains the growth.

- The branch carried the same rustix 1.1.5 → 1.1.6 bump (RUSTSEC-2026-0486) that `main` has since merged in #1494, so after merging `main` `rust/Cargo.lock` is identical to `main` and no longer part of this diff.

### Assumptions and limits

- The thresholds, 1/6 for a rival script and 1/10 for Spanish markers, were chosen so that all 19 real issues and the six synthetic cases are classified correctly. A very short mixed sentence can still go either way. For example, a one-line request with two Spanish words among five English words reads as Spanish. This is intended, because such a turn plausibly is Spanish. A single Spanish word decides only a text of at most two words ("Thanks, gracias" reads as Spanish, "Please fix the café bug in this issue" as English).
- Spanish is the only shared-script language with markers in the seed. A Latin-script language added later gets the same whole-word treatment from its rule, with no code change.
title: fix(language): answer an English issue in English: whole-word markers and prose-based work-item language (#1557)
